compounding_issues: Session 1 discarded the Flask auth seed entirely and rewrote it as an async WebSocket notification server — a clean-slate pivot rather than an incremental build on the seed
Client identity keyed on the ephemeral TCP source port is fragile (OS port reuse / NAT can collide) and this decision persisted through all 5 sessions without revisiting
Synchronous sqlite3 calls (MessageStore) run directly in the event loop — documented as 'short transactions' but it is a blocking-operation debt that every later session's persistence work stacked on

The flagship session-2 feature (channels/subscribe-unsubscribe) shipped with zero tests; channel-scoped delivery stayed untested through the entire story (session 5 only added tests for rate limiting and history)

Transport `_close_redis` and the `_redis_loop` cancellation handling are sloppy (`except (asyncio.CancelledError, Exception)` redundantly suppresses cancellation); session 3's Redis lifecycle code was never hardened
key_decisions: Full greenfield rewrite of the seed into a single-class async WebSocket notification server with a port-based client registry (session 1)
Use the ephemeral TCP source port as the client id to avoid a separate id-allocator/registry (session 1)
Adopt a channel subscription model with per-client channel sets plus read-only HTTP endpoints (/channels, /channels/<name>/subscribers) (session 2)
Add SQLite MessageStore for durable persistence and Redis pub/sub for multi-instance distribution, with graceful in-process fallback when Redis is unavailable (session 3)
Extract a BaseTransport ABC + WebSocketTransport to decouple the server from the websockets library and enable alternate transports via TRANSPORT env var (session 4)

Harden production concerns: Redis-backed + in-process fallback per-minute rate limiting, TTL-based retention with a daily cleanup loop, and a since-cursor history endpoint with has_more pagination (session 5)
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across the five sessions. Session 1 produced a minimal but clean 174-line server with two solid tests; session 2 added a real feature (channel subscriptions) but regressed in test discipline by shipping untested; session 3 sharply raised the bar by layering durable persistence and Redis multi-instance delivery with an integration test; session 4 was a genuinely architectural refactor (transport abstraction) that improved extensibility without breaking behavior; session 5 capped the arc with production hardening (rate limiting, message TTL cleanup, paginated history) and a restored test suite. Code grew from 174 to 529 lines while staying organized into clear classes (MessageStore, BaseTransport, WebSocketTransport, NotificationServer), and the final suite passes 5 with 1 skipped. A few rough edges (sync SQLite in the loop, port-based identity, catch-all exception handling) remain, but they are stable debts rather than accumulating rot — the trajectory is clearly upward and convergent.
